text: Wombats produce cube-shaped poop. They stack the little cubes on rocks and logs to mark their territory.
useIt: Next time someone says nature is boring

text: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
useIt: At the zoo, standing in front of the pink birds

text: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood. Two hearts pump blood through the gills, the third pumps it through the rest of the body.
useIt: When someone says they 'put their heart into it'

text: Botanically, bananas are berries, but strawberries are not.
useIt: When someone orders a berry smoothie

text: The Eiffel Tower can grow about 15 cm taller in summer, because the iron expands in the heat.
useIt: On a hot day in Paris (or anywhere, really)

text: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
useIt: When someone calls something 'ancient history'

text: The University of Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire. Teaching there began around 1096; Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325.
useIt: When someone brags about an old institution

text: A day on Venus (243 Earth days) is longer than its year (225 Earth days).
useIt: When a day at work feels like it lasts a year

text: The shortest war in recorded history, the Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896, lasted somewhere between 38 and 45 minutes.
useIt: When an argument ends surprisingly fast

text: The national animal of Scotland is the unicorn.
useIt: At a whisky tasting

text: The dot above a lowercase i or j is called a tittle.
useIt: When someone is being very picky about details

text: Sea otters sometimes hold hands while sleeping, so they don't drift away from each other.
useIt: On Valentine's Day

text: In 1947, engineers found a real moth stuck in a relay of the Harvard Mark II computer and taped it in the logbook as the 'first actual case of bug being found'.
useIt: When a programmer blames 'a bug'

text: Sharks are older than trees. Sharks appeared about 450 million years ago; the first trees about 385 million years ago.
useIt: When someone calls something 'as old as the trees'

text: Nintendo was founded in 1889, as a company that made playing cards.
useIt: During a game night

text: A 'jiffy' is a real unit of time. In electronics it is one cycle of the mains power: 1/50 or 1/60 of a second.
useIt: When someone says they'll be back 'in a jiffy'

text: Fredric Baur, who designed the Pringles can, asked for some of his ashes to be buried in one. His family honoured the request in 2008.
useIt: When someone opens a tube of crisps

text: Saturn is less dense than water. In a (very) big enough bathtub, it would float.
useIt: In the bath, obviously

text: There are more possible games of chess (around 10^120) than atoms in the observable universe (around 10^80).
useIt: When someone says chess is 'just a game'

text: Butterflies taste with their feet. Sensors on their legs tell them if a leaf is good to lay eggs on.
useIt: When someone won't try new food

text: The heart of a blue whale weighs around 180 kg, about as much as two adult men.
useIt: When someone says they have a big heart

text: Napoleon wasn't short. He was about 1.69 m, average or slightly above for a Frenchman of his time. British cartoonists made the myth.
useIt: When someone mentions a 'Napoleon complex'

text: Vikings almost certainly didn't wear horned helmets. That image comes mostly from 19th-century costume designs for Wagner's operas.
useIt: At a costume party

text: The Great Wall of China is not visible from the Moon with the naked eye. It is far too narrow.
useIt: When someone repeats the myth

text: A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh roughly a billion tonnes on Earth.
useIt: When someone says their bag is heavy

text: In the 1830s ketchup was sold in pill form as a medicine for indigestion.
useIt: When someone drowns their fries in ketchup

text: Carrots used to be mostly purple or yellow. Orange carrots were popularised by Dutch growers in the 17th century.
useIt: At dinner, holding a carrot

text: The # symbol has an official-sounding name: the octothorpe.
useIt: When someone says 'hashtag' out loud

text: Your body replaces the cells lining your stomach every few days, so the acid doesn't digest you.
useIt: After a very spicy meal

text: Koala fingerprints are so similar to human ones that, under a microscope, they are very hard to tell apart.
useIt: While watching a crime series

text: The first webcam watched a coffee pot. Researchers at Cambridge set it up in 1991 to see if the pot was empty without walking to it.
useIt: In the office kitchen

text: The Hundred Years' War lasted 116 years, from 1337 to 1453.
useIt: When a meeting runs way over time

text: An ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain.
useIt: When someone has a big idea and not much else

text: A bolt of lightning can reach about 30,000 °C, roughly five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
useIt: During a thunderstorm

text: Pluto hasn't completed a single orbit around the Sun since it was discovered in 1930. One orbit takes about 248 years.
useIt: When someone says they've been waiting forever

text: In 1386 a pig was put on trial in Falaise, France, for killing a child. It was found guilty and executed, dressed in human clothes.
useIt: When the legal system comes up

text: Sloths can hold their breath for up to 40 minutes, far longer than most dolphins.
useIt: At the swimming pool

text: The word 'muscle' comes from the Latin 'musculus', meaning 'little mouse', because a flexing muscle looked like a mouse moving under the skin.
useIt: At the gym

text: The Mona Lisa has no visible eyebrows or eyelashes.
useIt: In a museum, or at the make-up counter

text: Humans are the only animals known to blush.
useIt: When someone turns red
